unitemized.reason: The positive rule (always use parameterized queries/ORM) only applies when the run writes query code, which can't be expressed as an applies_when predicate. Its checkable part is covered by the unimplemented it-045 item.
Whether a label is 'meaningful' is a judgement call. It also only applies when form inputs are added, which no predicate can express.
Proper heading order in frontend markup only applies when markup is written, and no kind inspects markup structure.
This is a soft CSS preference ('prefer rem/em') that depends on the context. It only applies when CSS is written, and no kind inspects stylesheet content.
Consistent code style is relative to each repository's own conventions. No formatter is named, so there is no deterministic check.
Naming quality comes with a vague exception ('except in narrow contexts'), so it is a judgement call and can't be checked deterministically.
Consistent indentation is relative to each repository's own style. No kind inspects code formatting.

This is general advice about how to set up an editor or linter, not tied to any task in the run. Configuring a linter may also fall outside the spec's scope, so nothing in the run can show it was followed or broken.
